title: Lena and the Salt
premise: Lena, a salt-seller's daughter in the free city of Vell, discovers she can hear the old gods through the salt crusts on her family's pans — a gift that makes her the last living anchor of the broken covenant between realms. Emrys Dunmore, the disgraced last swordspeaker who once helped outlaw magic, becomes her reluctant protector when the usurper's witch-hunters come for her. Together with a found family of smugglers, exiled priests, and one very loyal goat, they must carry Lena to the drowned shrine at Greywater and reforge the covenant before the usurper's armies reach the free cities. In the end, Lena learns the covenant demands an inheritance of memory — and chooses to bind the gods not to bloodlines or oaths, but to freely given trust, shattering the usurper's claim and opening magic to all.
about_author: H. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime folklore along the northern coasts. Their debut novel grew out of a fascination with salt as both preservative and wound.

chapters.title: The Taste of Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. While selling salt in Vell's night market, Lena hears a voice through a crusted pan — an old god answering a stranger's desperate prayer. Terrified and exhilarated, she hides the pan rather than report it as the law demands. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by fear of discovery.

chapters.title: A Swordspeaker's Small Charms
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys sells illegal luck-charms, hollow and powerless, until one actually works — because Lena's awakened gift has leaked into his stock. Witch-hunters trace the flare of real magic to his stall. He flees, recognizing the signature of something he thought dead. Beat: guilt rekindled into dread.

chapters.title: Salt on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hunters raid Lena's home; her father burns the pans and is taken in her place. A scarred stranger — Emrys — pulls her out through the fish-cellars. She hates him for what oath-speakers did to end the old age. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Covenant
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pair joins the Brine Witches, a smuggler crew led by Captain Ossa, who once served Emrys's order. Around a galley fire, Lena demonstrates her gift and the crew swears informal loyalty to her — the first fragile found-family bond. Beat: belonging offered cautiously.

chapters.title: What the Usurper Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Interlude revealing the truth: three years ago Emrys broke the covenant under coercion, believing he was saving the free cities from a god-war. The usurper has been harvesting that brokenness to fuel his armies. Beat: shame confronted, loyalty to Lena deepening.

chapters.title: The Road of White Fields
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Ambushed on the salt flats, the crew loses their ship and Ossa is gravely wounded. Lena, panicking, calls too loudly to the gods — and every hunter within fifty miles hears the answer. Beat: the cost of power, first true sacrifice by a companion.

chapters.title: Lies Told in Good Faith
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lena discovers Emrys's role in breaking the covenant and confronts him mid-journey. Trust fractures; she nearly leaves with a rival guide offering safe passage. Ossa's quiet counsel about chosen family turns her back. Beat: loyalty versus truth, painfully weighed.

chapters.title: The Drowned Shrine at Greywater
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They reach the flooded shrine as the usurper's vanguard arrives. To open the gate, Lena must walk beneath the water carrying the memories of everyone who trusts her — a rite meant for dynasties, not a salt-girl. Beat: terror transfigured into acceptance.

chapters.title: An Inheritance Freely Given
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. In the shrine's depths, Lena reforges the covenant by binding it to consent rather than blood, while Emrys above holds the hunters off with the first true swordspeaking in three years, nearly dying. The gods rise; the usurper's claim collapses. Beat: sacrifice answered by grace.

chapters.title: Bread, Salt, and Open Doors
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue-near. Magic returns lawfully to the free cities; Emrys, recovering, takes up teaching instead of oaths. Lena returns to Vell with her father freed and her found family around her, selling salt that now sings softly to anyone willing to listen. Beat: home rebuilt, wider than before.
